messages:
maria-support: Hey team — customer reporting that their client SDK estimate is consistently ~3-6 tokens lower than what our API metering shows. They pasted a minimal repro and said invoice mismatch. attaching payload snippet.

maria-support: payload (redacted):
```json
{
  \"model\": \"redwood-1.2\",
  \"messages\": [
    {\"role\": \"system\", \"content\": \"You are a helpful assistant.\"},
    {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"Summarize the following: ...\"}
  ],
  \"functions\": [ { \"name\": \"lookup\", \"arguments\": { \"id\": \"123\" } } ]
}
```

maria-support: SDK v0.8.1 estimate says 128 tokens, API invoice shows 131. Customer says difference persists across different prompts.

chris-devex: thanks — do we know if the SDK estimator is including system messages / function call metadata? a lot of customers forget server-side system injection.

sanjay-billing: pinging billing — we see 131 on the meter for that request id. breakdown shows prompt: 45, completion: 86. estimator claiming prompt+completion 128 (split ~44/84).

tokenizer-bot: quick check: model redwood-1.2 uses BPE variant with invisible control token  that server injects for function_call boundaries. These are not always counted by local JS tokenizers unless you sync encoding tables.

oliver-eng-runtime: what else in the payload? are we streaming? function args can be returned in a serialized string that increases completion tokens if expanded on server. Also server may append a hidden suffix for routing (e.g., \uE000 markers) — should be counted.

maria-support: customer says they saw the extra tokens even with no stream and the same payload posted directly to our hosted API (curl). but their SDK estimate still lower.

chris-devex: two likely gaps: 1) SDK uses tokenizer mapping from model alias 'redwood-1.2' to encoding v3 but server used encoding v4 after hotfix; 2) SDK estimator omits system-inserted tool call framing tokens (we recently added a 3-token boundary for function_call framing).

sanjay-billing: I've pulled the per-request logs for that request id. server logs show \"system_inserted: true\" and function_call framing tokens: +3. meter calculation comment: \"counted control tokens for routing and function framing\".

maria-support: customer asks whether this is a bug (overbilling) or mismatch (estimator out of date).

oliver-eng-runtime: it's an estimator drift issue. runtime team rolled a tiny change (adds a 3-token framing sequence around function calls) to improve alignment. SDK estimates need to adopt the same encoding / framing rules. No overbilling — meter reflects actual bytes our runtime processed.

chris-devex: workaround: SDK consumers can set header X-include-system-tokens: true to let estimator include server-side system-inserts in local calc. that's in SDK >=0.8.3 which we just cut. Can you ask customer to upgrade to 0.8.3 and re-run?

maria-support: relaying — customer on older pinned SDK in prod. will they need code changes?

oliver-eng-runtime: no code changes required, just upgrade. estimator will now map redwood-1.2 -> encoding v4 and add function framing tokens. If they can't upgrade, we can provide a simple patch: add +3 tokens to completion estimate when functions array present and include system messages.

tokenizer-bot: note: also watch for tool-returned JSON. When functions return nested json strings we escape quotes which add tokens on server tokenization vs naive char-counting in some client estimates.

sanjay-billing: marking as "estimator drift" for billing ops. no invoice adjustments for past invoices; if customer wants, we can do a one-off credit after SOC approval, but default is no change when meter matches runtime.

maria-support: customer accepted upgrade path. they'll test on staging and report back. thanks all. :raised_hands:

billing-bot: Invoice check queued — if the customer requests credit, open support case BC-3942.

maria-support: closing loop — will reopen if upgrade doesn't fix.
